description: Fragment of a clay tablet; top right corner. prayer or incantation to a god. 14 lines of inscription, Neo-Assyrian.

references.notes: +WL Rm-II.328 +WL Rm-II.477) K 16694 Lambert AfO 27 76f. Rm 2,328 + Rm-II.477 Cagni Epopea und Erra-Epos Tf. I. Rm-II.328 Lambert ZA 54 245, {FWG D 21}. Rm-II. 477 Lambert AfO 18 397, {FWG T 69}..

Boxes like these \[i.e. boxes holding unnumbered fragments of the K type\] must have been the source of many fragments included by L. W. King in the first Supplement to the Kouyunjik Catalogue, in addition to those from new excavations of 1904-1905 and a few obtained in other ways. His fragments had previously been considered “of too small an importance to justify their inclusion in the numbered collection of tablets” (King 1914: xv). They number K14231-K16794 which is a respectable quantity. While all those chosen by King were then assigned K numbers, he noted where they had belonged to groups such as Rm 2 and 81-2-4, helpful information since there is slightly better information about the provenance of these later groups.

document.title: The 1975 Kouyunjik Colophon Project and its Consequences for the Collection
